observations: body L2-L7: the c of «adn. c» (L2) is bold italic; «Albatenio» (L7) is letter-spaced. The o of «Interpolatorem» (L4) prints only as a sliver, and the l of «planetarum» (L4) prints broken, like an apostrophe.
body L8-L10: «al–Battānī» (L8) is letter-spaced; «al–Battānī» (L8, L10) has long dashes (5.5 and 5.3 pt).

body L12-L20: the head «Diametrus apparens» is in a small bold type (x-height 4.6 pt, against 4.9 pt in the rows), the heads of the columns in a smaller bold type (x-height 3.4 pt), with a brace under the head over the three columns; the numbers stand on their right edges. With al-Battānī's distances (translation, pp. 120-122: Mercury 64ᵖ 10′, 115, 166; Venus 166, 618, 1070; Mars 1146, 4584, 8022; Jupiter 8022, 10473, 12924; Saturn 12924, 15509, 18094) and his diameters at the mean distances, 1/15, 1/10, 1/20, 1/12 and 1/18 of 32′ 30″ (2′ 10″, 3′ 15″, 1′ 37″ ½, 2′ 42″ ½, 1′ 48″ ⅓), the apparent diameters, inversely as the distances, are: Mercury 1′ 30″ and 3′ 53″ (3′ 54″ with 64ᵖ for 64ᵖ 10′); Venus 1′ 53″ and 12′ 6″; Mars 0′ 56″ and 6′ 30″; Jupiter 2′ 12″ and 3′ 32″; Saturn 1′ 33″ and 2′ 10″, as printed, the halves of the mean diameters of Mars and Jupiter being dropped. The Sun (31′ 20″, 32′ 30″, 33′ 40″) and the Moon (29′ 30″, 32′ 25″, 35′ 20″) are al-Battānī's diameters of p. 58 of the translation and their means.

body L21: the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 8.6 pt; a heavy bracket closes Schiaparelli's addition, opened on p. 290, L38. The feet of the two L of «Schiaparelli» print apart from their stems, as on p. 290, L24.
body L22-L25: «20–30», «al–Muqātil» and «al–Kātib» have long dashes (5.3, 5.5 and 5.5 pt). The t of «al–Muqātil» did not print but for the top of its stem, like an apostrophe.

body L28-L34: «Dozy», «al–Akhḍarī», divided between L31 and L32, «al–Wānsharīshī» and «az–Zarqālī» are letter-spaced; «boreo–occidenta-», «Latino–Arabico», «al–Akh-», «al–Wānsharīshī», «Arabico–Hispani» and «az–Zarqālī» have long dashes (5.2, 5.4, 5.3, 5.5, 5.3 and 5.3 pt). A dot stands under the a of «al–Wānsharīshī» (L32), like ạ. Addenda, p. LXXVI («291,7 a f.», L32): other examples of al-kātib and al-mukātib for Mercury and of al-muqātil for Saturn occur throughout the Moroccan Muḥammad as-Sūsī al-Marghitī, al-Mumta‘ fī sharḥ al-maqna‘ and al-Maṭla‘ ‘alà masā’il al-maqna‘ (both in one volume, Fez 1313 H.; cf. p. 205, note 1).
body L38: the n of «in» before «fine» prints with a broken right stem.
notes_left L1-L3: «Latino-Arabicum» and «15-17» have hyphens (3.2 and 3.1 pt).

notes_left L4-L6: «Saḥnūn al–Wānsharīshī» and «al-Akhḍarī» are letter-spaced; the dash of the first measures 4.3 pt, that of the second 3.1 pt, a hyphen like those of «al-muḥtāǵ», «53-56» and «ar-Raḥmān». The dots after «‘alà» are five; the dash before «‘Abd» measures 7.9 pt.
notes_right L1-L3: «-Akhḍarī» repeats the hyphen of «al-» at the end of the left column. The month Dhū ’l-qa‘dah 939 of the Hiǵrah ran from 25 May to 23 June 1533 (Julian, by the tabular calendar).

notes_right L5-L6: «Arçhachelis» is letter-spaced. Addenda, pp. LXXVI-LXXVII («291, adn. 3»): from Steinschneider, Zum Speculum astronomicum (Zeitschr. f. Mathem. XVI, 1871, p. 390), Nallino later learned that Arçachel is a corruption of Zahel, i.e. Sahl ibn Bishr, not az-Zarqālī; the Laurentian codex S. Marco 194 (f. 69 r.-87 v.) begins «Incipit liber arçachelis introductorius ad librum iudiciorum arabum», with «almicatil [al-muqātil] .i. saturnus».
